version.description: Version 2 is what this project writes; version 1 is accepted as input. A settings.json written before the settings application existed has no glass, fonts, startup or app section, and configstore.load merges the defaults underneath it, so refusing a version 1 document would refuse every existing install. The migration that upgrades one lives in iarch/settings-app/iarch_settings/services/config_store.py as migrate_v1_to_v2, and tests/test_settings_config_store.py proves a version 1 document comes out of it as a version 2 document that validates.

theme.description: The design-system selection iarch-theme renders from, added in Part 2. It sits alongside the coarse Part-1 'preset' master switch and the 'effects' toggles rather than replacing them: 'colour_preset' names one of the palettes in data/design/presets/ (validated at runtime against that directory, so the list stays open), and 'intensity' names one of the four the tokens define. configstore.load merges the repository default under a user's file, so a settings.json written before this block existed still resolves a theme. iarch-theme apply writes both keys back here; reconciling them with the coarse 'preset'/'effects' switches is Part 4 settings-app work.

colour_mode.description: What this application and the shell agree on. Applied through the shell's theme-mode-set verb and through gtk-application-prefer-dark-theme, so the two cannot drift: one value, two projections, written together.

accent.description: An accent override as #rrggbb, or an empty string to follow the colour preset's own accent role. Empty is the default because a preset that has passed the contrast gate should not be second-guessed by a value that has not; when it is set, the contrast gate is run again before anything is written.

animation.description: The motion state iarch-anim renders from, added in Part 3. It is deliberately separate from 'theme': a theme is a look (colour preset plus intensity) and this is how that look moves, so a person can be on frosted glass and bouncy motion, or on the Performance intensity — which pairs with the 'off' preset — without either choice overwriting the other. 'preset' names a file in data/design/animations/, 'speed' is the global multiplier where a number above 1 is FASTER because it divides every duration, 'reduce_motion' forces the minimal preset with every duration capped, and 'event_overrides' maps an animation leaf to whether the user turned it on or off on top of whatever the preset declares. The overrides are keyed by leaf name, which is an open set the compositor defines rather than one this schema can enumerate, so the values are constrained to booleans here and the names are checked against data/design/animations.json at render time. Not in the top-level 'required' list on purpose: configstore.load merges these defaults under a settings.json written before this block existed, so an older user file still resolves and still validates. The 0.5 and 2.0 bounds duplicate tokens.json motion.animation.speed_multiplier because a schema cannot read another file; tests/test_animation_presets.py asserts the two agree.

modes.description: The two mode switches added in Part 3: iarch-gamemode and iarch-focus. A mode records whether it is on and, while it is, the state it replaced -- which is what makes it reversible instead of merely another way to change a setting. Game mode's restore point is a theme and a motion preset, so it survives a relogin and only `iarch-gamemode off` ends it; focus mode's is the Do Not Disturb flag and two compositor leaves, which are runtime state and die with the session, so `iarch-focus status` compares the record with what the shell and the compositor actually answer rather than trusting it. Not in the top-level required list, for the same reason as theme and animation: configstore.load merges these defaults under a settings.json written before the block existed. The two enums duplicate theme.intensity and animation.preset above because a schema cannot read another key, and tests/test_gamemode.py asserts the three lists agree.

do_not_disturb.description: What notification-dnd-status answered before focus mode was switched on. Null means the shell could not be asked, and `off` then says so instead of claiming it restored a state it never read.

leaves.description: The compositor leaves focus mode replaced, keyed by leaf name, each with the value it had before. A null is a leaf that could not be read, which also means it could not be set.

glass.description: The Glass page. leaves holds overrides on top of the intensity the theme renders: the key is a Hyprland config leaf exactly as data/design/tokens.json spells it under hyprland.leaves, and the value is inside that record's range. An empty object means the intensity's own values, which is what a fresh install has. per_app_opacity is an ordered list of window-class regexes and the opacity to give them, added to the rules the tokens' app_classes groups already produce. Neither is a second source of truth for an intensity: an override says 'this leaf, this value, on top of whatever the intensity decided', and clearing the section returns to the intensity exactly.

leaves.description: Leaf name to value. The schema cannot enumerate the leaves because they belong to the compositor's record, so the authority is data/design/tokens.json: hyprland.leaves for the names, hyprland.integer_leaves for which ones are whole numbers and hyprland.ranges for the bounds. tests/test_settings_glass.py checks every key and value against that record, which is where a leaf that does not exist gets caught.

class.description: A window class. Anchored and escaped by the renderer the way data/design/tokens.json's app_classes patterns are, so a value here is a plain class name or a simple regex body, not a full pattern.

fonts.description: The Fonts & Icons page. Every key maps to one GtkSettings property recorded in data/design/gtk-settings.json, and the projection is ~/.config/gtk-4.0/settings.ini plus ~/.config/gtk-3.0/settings.ini. An empty string or a zero means 'do not write this key at all', which leaves the system default in place -- a font the user never chose must not be pinned, because pinning one stops the session's own font change from reaching GTK applications.

ui_family.description: The family part of gtk-font-name. Empty leaves the design tokens' Inter in place.

size_pt.description: The size part of gtk-font-name, in points. 0 means do not write the key.

antialias.description: gtk-xft-antialias, written as 1 or 0. The key's third value, -1, is the system default and is what not writing the key means.

hint_style.description: gtk-xft-hintstyle. The four spellings GTK compares with strcmp; anything else is ignored rather than refused, so the page offers a dropdown and no free text.

subpixel.description: gtk-xft-rgba, the subpixel order. Same silent-ignore behaviour as the hint style.

icon_theme.description: gtk-icon-theme-name. Empty means do not write the key.

cursor_theme.description: gtk-cursor-theme-name. Empty means do not write the key.

cursor_size.description: gtk-cursor-theme-size. 0 is the key's own 'system default' value and also means do not write it.

startup.description: The Startup & Default apps page's autostart list. Each entry becomes one ~/.config/autostart/iarch-<name>.desktop file, which is the mechanism a session without a display manager still honours. This application writes the file and never runs the command: the session runs it, at startup, exactly as it would a .desktop file the user wrote by hand. The default apps are deliberately not here -- they belong to ~/.config/mimeapps.list, which xdg-mime owns, and a copy in this file could disagree with it.

name.description: Becomes the file's stem, so it is restricted to characters that are safe in a filename on every filesystem this project supports.

command.description: The Exec= value. Written verbatim into the .desktop file and never executed by this application, so it is not passed through a shell here; the session's own launcher parses it the way it parses any autostart entry.

enabled.description: False writes the entry with Hidden=true rather than deleting it, so turning a program back on does not need its command retyped.

app.description: This application's own state: the window it opens and the page it opens on.

last_page.description: A page id from the registry in iarch/settings-app/iarch_settings/pages/__init__.py. Not an enum here, because the schema would then have to be edited every time a page is added, and an unknown id is already handled: the window opens on Home and says nothing about a page that no longer exists.

display.description: The Display page. One entry per monitor the user configured, rendered into ~/.config/hypr/monitors.lua by iarch/cli/gen_monitors_lua.py. An empty list is the shipped default and means the identity rule -- output "", mode preferred, position auto, scale 1 -- which matches every output and is why a fresh install works on hardware nobody has seen. The shapes below are the ones the compositor's own parser accepts; the bounds and the field list are in data/design/monitors.json, and the generator refuses a value that record does not allow rather than emitting a line the compositor answers with a config error at login. Nothing the compositor reports about a monitor is stored here: the page reads `hyprctl -j monitors` and shows that, so there is no second copy of a resolution or a refresh rate to go stale.

output.description: The output name exactly as `hyprctl -j monitors` reported it (DP-1, HDMI-A-2, eDP-1). Restricted to characters that are safe inside a Lua string and inside a filename.

mode.description: A resolution, optionally with a refresh rate. The spellings come from parseMode in src/config/shared/monitor/Parser.cpp at v0.57.2, and the optional Hz suffix is there because availableModes prints `WxH@RR.RRHz` and parseMode reads the rate with stof, which stops at the first character that is not part of a number; the generator additionally requires a WxH form to be one the compositor listed in availableModes, so a resolution nobody can drive is refused here rather than tried on the hardware.

position.description: Either one of the nine auto spellings parsePosition accepts, or an XxY offset. An offset without the x is refused by the parser, which is why the pattern requires it.

scale.description: A string, not a number: MONITOR_FIELDS builds this field with CLuaConfigString, so `scale = 1` unquoted is a parse error. parseScale refuses a value below 0.25 and resets it to 1, and the generator refuses it first with a message that says so.

transform.description: The wl_output_transform enumeration. 0 is normal, then the three rotations and the four flipped forms.

disabled.description: Switch the output off. The generator refuses to disable the last enabled monitor, because a monitor that is off cannot show the dialog that offers to turn it back on.
